title: Generative AI
subtitle: Diffusion, and everything built on top of it

slides.title: Why this module exists
bullets: An LLM already IS a generative model: samples from P(next token)
This module widens the lens to pixels, video, and audio
One family now dominates all three: diffusion
Target: train a real (tiny) diffusion model from scratch, no hand-waving
slides.notes: Frame this as Module 03/04's generative idea, applied to a continuous signal instead of discrete tokens.

slides.title: The generative family tree
rows: factorise P(x), generate one unit at a time
learn to reverse a noising process
slides.notes: Normalizing flows exist too but haven't scaled - mention in passing if asked.

slides.title: Why diffusion won
bullets: Diffusion training is plain regression: predict the noise you added
No adversary, no minimax game, no mode collapse by construction
That is exactly why it scaled to internet-size data with no babysitting
Price: sampling needs tens-to-hundreds of network passes, not one
Opinion: default to diffusion (or flow matching) unless you have a reason not to
slides.notes: GANs still win a narrow set of real-time single-domain tasks - name one if asked, e.g. face reenactment.

slides.title: Forward process: destroy the image on a schedule
bullets: x_t = sqrt(1-beta_t)*x_(t-1) + sqrt(beta_t)*eps, repeated T times
No learning required here - it is arithmetic, governed by a schedule
Closed form: x_t = sqrt(abar_t)*x0 + sqrt(1-abar_t)*eps
This closed form is why training needs no simulation loop
Pick a random x0, random t, one eps -> one training example, one line
slides.notes: Emphasize the closed-form jump - it is the single most important equation in the whole module.

slides.title: Reverse process: learn to undo it
bullets: Train a network eps_theta(x_t, t) to predict the noise that was added
Loss: mean squared error between predicted and true noise
Same supervised training loop as Module 01, extra input: a random timestep
Sampling: start from pure noise, iteratively subtract predicted noise
Small steps matter - one big leap produces a blurry average, not sharp detail
slides.notes: Tie the 'blurry average' failure directly back to why VAEs blur - same underlying math.

slides.title: DDPM vs DDIM sampling
slides.notes: code/guidance_and_sampling.py measures this exact table numerically - show the printed output.

slides.title: Classifier-free guidance
bullets: Conditioning directly, eps_theta(x_t,t,c), tends to be soft
Fix: randomly drop the condition during training (~10% of examples)
At sampling time, run the network twice: conditioned and unconditioned
eps_guided = eps_u + w * (eps_c - eps_u), w is the guidance scale
No separate classifier needed - the trick is in training, not sampling
slides.notes: This is the CFG-scale slider in every text-to-image tool - name it explicitly.

slides.title: Guidance scale: fidelity up, diversity down
slides.notes: code/guidance_and_sampling.py's Q2 sweep produces this table's numbers on a toy dataset - no free lunch.

slides.title: Latent diffusion: why Stable Diffusion is not pixel-space
bullets: Diffusing 512x512x3 pixels directly: huge cost per reverse step
Train a VAE to compress images into a small latent grid, e.g. 64x64x4
Run the entire diffusion process in that latent space instead
Only the final step decodes the latent back to pixels
Roughly an order of magnitude in compute, small usually-imperceptible cost
slides.notes: Draw the pipeline: image -> VAE encoder -> latent -> diffusion -> latent -> VAE decoder -> image.

slides.title: The architecture shift: U-Net to DiT
slides.notes: Same story as CNN-to-transformer in vision classification - the field has seen this shift before.

slides.title: Text-to-image, end to end
bullets: Text encoder (CLIP, or a full LLM/T5 encoder in newer systems)
Cross-attention: image latent patches query the text token embeddings
Scheduler: picks the noise schedule and step-update rule, swappable
Negative prompts are CFG again - guided away from a named unwanted thing
Seed + deterministic sampler = reproducible image, the basis of seed hunting
slides.notes: CLIP's 77-token limit and bag-of-concepts style is why newer systems add a T5/LLM encoder.

slides.title: img2img, inpainting, ControlNet
bullets: img2img: start from a real image partially noised, not from pure noise
Inpainting: reset unmasked pixels to their correct noise level each step
ControlNet: a trained side-network injects a structural signal per step
Structural signal examples: edge map, depth map, pose skeleton
Decouples what (text controls content) from where (control signal controls layout)
slides.notes: ControlNet is arguably the single biggest production unlock - text alone is a poor spatial interface.

slides.title: Video and audio: same idea, harder substrate
bullets: Independent per-frame diffusion fails: flicker, morphing, no agreement
Fix: temporal attention, or spacetime patches (Sora's approach)
A 5-second clip at 24fps is roughly 120x an image's worth of pixels
Audio: autoregressive codec tokens vs diffusion over a mel-spectrogram
Voice cloning needs only seconds of reference audio in modern systems
slides.notes: Consistency failures - flicker, an object changing identity - are video's version of six-fingered hands.

slides.title: Multimodal models: understanding vs generating
bullets: LLaVA recipe: frozen CLIP vision encoder + small projection + an LLM
Projected image patches become extra tokens in the LLM's input sequence
The LLM's attention does not care what produced a token's embedding
Seeing and generating are separate capabilities - do not conflate them
Frontier direction: native multimodal training on interleaved tokens from scratch
slides.notes: Ask two separate questions about any system: can it see what I upload, and can it make me an image.

slides.title: Evaluation: every metric here is unsatisfying
slides.notes: Same unsolved problem as Module 15 for text - no scalar captures realism, fidelity, diversity, and correctness at once.

slides.title: The diagnostic that still works
slides.quote: Look at hands and text - both remain reliable tells for diffusion-generated content.
bullets: Hands: high-degrees-of-freedom structure, hard to learn from 2D projections
Rendered text: exact discrete symbols from a continuous process, no notion of spelling
Hallucinated detail is the image analogue of an LLM hallucination
slides.notes: Overall photorealism is hard to distinguish from real photos - hands and text still give it away.

slides.title: Failure modes, provenance, and the law
bullets: Mode collapse (GANs): sample 100 seeds, look for near-duplicates
C2PA metadata and invisible watermarks (SynthID) are friction, not guarantees
Deepfakes and voice cloning push impersonation to near-zero marginal cost
Training data licensing and output copyright are two separate open questions
US Copyright Office: bare prompt-and-click output is not copyrightable
slides.notes: C2PA metadata is stripped by any tool that does not preserve it, including a plain screenshot.

slides.title: Your exit check
bullets: Run code/diffusion_from_scratch.py and code/guidance_and_sampling.py unmodified
Explain every printed number: forward std, denoiser MSE floor, DDIM steps, guidance sweep
Sketch the DDPM training loop and the CFG sampling equation on a whiteboard, unaided
Then: Module 06 - AI Agents
slides.notes: The whiteboard sketch is the real test - if the equation only lives in the code, you are not done yet.
